Procedure: Washing tension insulators live using a mobile washing unit
Next review date: December 2010

This document sets out the procedures for washing tension insulators on towers of 66 kV using a mobile washing unit. The document was prepared by Eng. Karam Gouda Mohamed of the Ismailia Lines Department, reviewed by Eng. Mohamed Nasr Mohamed, Manager of the Ismailia Lines Department, approved by Eng. Abdel Aziz Attia Abou El-Fotouh, General Manager of West Canal Lines, and revised by Eng. Mohamed Omran (for the General Manager of Development and Quality Control). It was field-tested by Eng. Mohamed Moslem Salem on the Shabab Generation / Shabab 2 line on 2 February 2005, approved by Eng. Farag Ali El-Azab, Head of the West Canal Networks Sector, and the document was approved after adding the amendments agreed during the meeting of the MPIS coordinators on 27 December 2005.

A work order must be issued including the names of the workers, the date, time and place of work, the line name and tower number; if the work location is very far away, the work supervisor may issue the work order by telephone signal.

Every item of equipment at the work location and the resistivity of the water used shall be recorded in the work order; the resistivity value shall not be less than 1300 ohm/cm, or the conductivity shall not exceed 769 micro-mho (Siemens). No solvents shall be added to the water used in the washing process.

The workers must pass an annual examination in live washing, to make sure they fully understand how to use each item of equipment and understand and are able to complete the washing process; this examination shall be recorded in the workers' register and in each person's occupational safety and health card.
Any drop in water pressure requires the water jet to be directed away from the insulator, conductor and tower.
It is essential to make sure communication is achieved between the work supervisor and the nearest station to the work location.
Make sure there are no broken discs in the insulators; washing shall not be carried out if the number of broken discs exceeds one third of the total number of discs in the insulator string.

All the values stated in the technical procedures shall be applied, concerning: the nozzle diameter, the water pressure on the pump (27 bar), the length of the water jet, the resistivity of the water insulation, the hose length, the angle of inclination of the jet to the string, the minimum distance between the nozzle and the conductor: 2.74 m.

Work must be stopped in the following cases: rain, lightning, thunder, storms or fog, or if the wind speed exceeds 10 m/s, or at nightfall, or when visibility decreases, or upon disconnection caused by the washing process or for any other reason.
Workers shall avoid any equipment or wet ground during washing.

Work must be stopped if the wind speed exceeds the following values: - For washing tension insulators with an angle up to 20 degrees (8 m/s) - For washing tension insulators with an angle from 20 to 45 degrees (6 m/s) - For washing tension insulators with an angle over 45 degrees (4 m/s)
All workers shall stand away from the earthed equipment at a distance of not less than 2 m.

sections_target.text: Instructions the work supervisor must follow before going to the site:

rows: Determine the type of equipment to be used according to the nature of the terrain (agricultural tractor with trailer, small unit, transport truck).
Make sure the tank is filled with water.
Make sure the water hoses are sound (not cracked, not punctured, the assembly couplings tightly fastened, the hoses or the nozzle not blocked).

Make sure the pump engine is sound (carburettor, distributor, battery, fuel tank, radiator water), checking this with the competent workshop; the team then starts the engine and makes sure it is sound before going to the site.
Make sure the pump is sound (the pump packing is sound, to obtain the required pressure).
Make sure the nozzle earth and the equipment (truck) earth are sound (no cut in the earth cable, and the earth clamps tightly fastened to the cables).

sections_target.text: Instructions the work supervisor must follow upon arriving at the site:

rows: The person in charge of the work determines the wind speed and direction, and accordingly determines the suitable place for the washing equipment next to the tower according to the wind direction and determines the sequence of work.
The washing unit equipment shall be earthed well to the tower body.

The technician assigned to operate the water machine runs the machine for not less than 5 minutes before preparing the machine to pump water (if the pump engine runs on petrol), and the water tank cover is opened.
The person in charge of the work measures the water resistance.
The linesman climbs the tower carrying (pulley, service rope, sling, weight).
He fixes the pulley at the top middle of the tower, at the level of the stay of the second travelling platform.
After fixing the pulley on the tower, he hangs the weight at the end of the service rope and lowers it from inside the tower formations.
The hose is fixed with a sling, leaving 3 m of hose at the fixing point.
The washing man takes his place between the two circuits at the level of the first travelling platform, and the nozzle earth is tied to the tower body.
The linesman gives the start signal to operate the pump and pump water into the hose.
The linesman tests the water jet away from the insulator, conductor and tower, then starts washing phases T then S for both circuits in the first direction, according to the wind direction.
After finishing washing phases T and S for both circuits, the nozzle earth is removed from the tower and the linesman climbs to the level of the second travelling platform.
The nozzle earth is tied to the tower body, and washing of phase R for both circuits begins, according to the wind direction, as shown in the drawing.
After finishing washing phase R, the nozzle earth is removed and he descends to the level of the first travelling platform.
Move to the other side of the tower and start washing phases T, then S, then R, repeating steps 7, 6, 5.

The linesman gives a signal to stop the washing pump and starts removing the nozzle earth and lowering the hose with the service rope, making sure no equipment is left inside the work area; the washing of a 66 kV tension tower is thus complete.
The linesman removes the pulley and the service rope and comes down with them, making sure no equipment is left inside the work area; the washing of a 66 kV tension tower is thus complete.
